CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  ECONOMIC AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT
  PLANNING COMMISSION
  MEETING AGENDA
July 7, 2021 7:00 P.M.
City Council Chambers – Ninth Floor (Planning Commission & Staff)
1 West Manchester Boulevard

  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS

Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social
distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant to the
Governor’s  Executive  Order  N-29-20(https://www.gov.ca.gov/wp-
content/uploads/2020/03/3.17.20-N-29-20-EO.pdf), please note that
members of the public will only be allowed to observe and address
the Planning Commission Meeting of July 7, 2021 at 7:00 P.M. by
telephone, video and other electronic means, as follows:

Viewing and Listening to the Meeting without Making Public Comments:
   On Spectrum Cable Local Channel 35 with audio and limited
  video. Please check with your cable provider for details.
   Live on-line through Facebook Live, with audio and limited
  video, at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/
   The above access options provide the public with the
  opportunity to both observe and listen to the meeting.
   However, members of the public who wish to orally address the
  Planning Commission must use the public access options noted
  below:

Listening to the Meeting and Making Oral Public Comments: Members
of the public may listen and make oral public comments
telephonically by dialing:

  Dial-in: 1-888-251-2949 or 215-861-0694
  Access Code: 4771429# wait 2 seconds and press # again

Please observe the following tips when phoning in:

    When you call-in, the operator will provide further
  instructions on how you can make public comments via phone.
    If you are calling from a cell phone, please call from an
  area with good reception.
    If you are watching the meeting on Facebook or Channel 35 while
  also accessing the phone line, it is requested that you mute
  the sound of your video feed as it is offset by 3 seconds from
  the phone transmission. Additionally, when you are making
  public comments on the phone line you will be inaudible due to
  feedback.

Written Public Comments: Members of the public can submit comments
for consideration by the Planning Commission by sending them to
Mindy  Wilcox,  AICP,  Planning  Manager  at
mwilcox@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure distribution to the members
of the Planning Commission prior to consideration of the agenda,
comments must be received prior to 12:00 P.M. on July 7, 2021, the
day of the meeting. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date
and agenda item. Comments received after 12:00 P.M. and prior to
close of the public hearing will be made part of the official public
record of the meeting.
[Agenda Items and Additional Public Access Options Listed on
Following Pages]
 1.  Pledge of Allegiance.

6.  PUBLIC HEARINGS
  a. A public hearing to consider an application by J. D. Fox,
  representing WDR, LLC, for AT&T, for Special Use Permit No.
  2021-007 (SP-2021-007) to allow the location of a roof-
  mounted wireless telecommunication facility on the roof of
  an existing parking garage on an approximately 3.6-acre,
  HPSP(Hollywood Park Specific Plan) zoned property at 3863
  West Century Boulevard.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm the categorical exemption EA-CE-2021-055; and
  2) Adopt the attached resolution approving SP-2021-007,
  subject to 15 conditions, and/or add conditions as
  deemed appropriate.

  b. A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment 2021-001
  (ZCA-2021-001) to Chapter 12 of the Inglewood Municipal
  Code to modify regulations for Smoke Shops.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2021-020; and
  2) Adopt a resolution recommending City Council adoption
  of Zoning Code Amendment ZCA-2021-001.

  c. A public hearing to consider Zoning Code Amendment 2021-004

  This item is requested by staff to be postponed to the
  September 1, 2021 Planning Commission meeting.

7.  NON - PUBLIC HEARINGS
  a. A non-public hearing to consider an application by Sandy
  Sigal, representing NewMark Merrill Companies, for Design
  Review No. 2021-005 (DR-2021-005) to allow a 936 square-foot
  mural on the exterior of a one-story commercial building
  that is part of an existing shopping center on an
  approximately  17-acre,  C-2(General  Commercial)  zoned
  property at 2876 West Imperial Highway.
  Preliminary Recommendations:
  1) Affirm Categorical Exemption EA-CE-2021-074; and
  2) Adopt a resolution approving DR-2021-005 subject to
  conditions.

8.  Commission Initiatives.

9.  Public Comments. Anyone wishing to address the Planning
  Commission on any matter within their jurisdiction and not

   MINUTES
  INGLEWOOD SPECIAL PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  TUESDAY, MARCH 11, 2020

(1) PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

The City of Inglewood Planning Commission held its Special Planning
Commission meeting on Tuesday, March 11, 2020, in the Community
Room, on the first floor, in City Hall. Following the Pledge of
Allegiance by Commissioner David Rice, the meeting was called to
order at 7:05 p.m.

(2) ROLL CALL:

Present:  Chairman Larry Springs
  Commissioner Patricia Patrick
  Commissioner David Rice
  Commissioner Aide Trejo
  Commissioner Terry Coleman

Staff:  Mindy Wilcox, AICP Planning Manager
  Eddy Ikemefuna, Senior Planner
  Fred Jackson, Senior Planner
  Jeff Lewis, Assistant City Attorney
  Bernard McCrumby, Planner
  Marissa Fewell, Assistant Planner
  Taylor Kay, Assistant Planner
  Evangeline Lane, Secretary

(3) STAFF COMMUNICATIONS:

Ms. Wilcox, Planning Manager stated that all of the items on
tonight’s agenda have corrections and/or changes that will be
addressed by each planner as they make their presentations this
evening.

(4) PUBLIC COMMENTS:

None

(5) MINUTES APPROVAL:

Commissioner Rice made the motion to approve the minutes of October
19, 2019 and was seconded by Chairman Springs.

MOTION:

The motion did not pass with the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Rice, and Chairman Springs.

Abstained: Commissioners Patrick, Trejo and Coleman

There was a new motion from Commissioner Rice to Continue the
Approval to the next Planning Commission Meeting, and was seconded
by Chairman Springs.

MOTION:

The motion did not pass with the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick,  Rice,  Trejo,  Coleman,  and
  Chairman Springs.
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 11, 2020

(6) PUBLIC HEARINGS:

6A: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-008 (SP-2019-008), 903 SOUTH
PRAIRIE AVENUE.
A public hearing to consider an application by Martin Gonzalez,
representing Getting Faded, for Special Use Permit No. 2019-008
(SP-2019-008) to allow a barber shop, within 300 feet of a similar
use, in an existing shopping center on a 34,697 square-foot C-2
(General Commercial) zoned property, at 903 South Prairie Avenue.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff:
 About the number of days of operation, will the shop be open
  for a full seven (7) days, will there be any days that the
  shop will be closed?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that at this time, the applicant would
  be the one to speak to that, but currently that is what is
  proposed.

Commissioner Rice asked staff:
 What about the number of chairs inside of the shop, as when he
  looked inside he counted a total of Thirteen (13), isn’t it
  supposed to be only eleven (11)?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that there are only eleven chairs drawn
  on the plans and for the layout of the shop, possibly the
  applicant can further address this.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff:
 Would like to have No Loitering Signs applied to the business
  area, along with more security cameras, and wanted to clarify
  the number of chairs in the building, would it be eleven chairs
  for cutting/styling and two at the wash bowls? Can we get
  clarification?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that it is only the eleven (11) chairs
  in the entire shop and that the bowls were not considered
  in the calculation.

Commissioner Coleman asked staff:
 Wanted to inquire about the number of security cameras on the
  premises and how many shops are there at the addressed location,
  as it is a strip-mall setup?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that there are seven other businesses in
  the center.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward to address
the Planning Commission and speak about his project.

Mr. & Mrs. Martin and Norma Gonzalez came and addressed the
planning commission about how they plan on operating the shop.

Ms. Gonzalez stated that the days of operation would be no more
than six (6) days, because it would be closed on Sunday, and
possibly closed on Mondays, which means that it will only be open
for five (5) days of operation.

Chairman Springs opened the floor for the planning commission to
address the applicant. There were no questions.
Chairman Springs opened the public hearing to the audience to speak
either for or against this project.
  2
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 11, 2020
FOR: / AGAINST:

None

Chairman Springs closed the public hearing and asked for any final
comments from the commissioners.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff:
 Can we add two more conditions to what is already in place?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated yes.

Chairman Springs called for the motion.

MOTION:

Commissioner Rice made the motion to affirm the categorical
exemption EA-CE-2020-026, and to adopt the attached resolution
approving SP-2019-008 subject to 10 conditions with two
additional conditions, 1) to add more security cameras and 2) to
post no loitering signs on the exterior and interior of the
business, and was seconded by Commissioner Coleman, Resolution
1857
  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA, APPROVING A
  CERTAIN SPECIAL USE PERMIT TO MARTIN GONZALEZ,
  TO ALLOW A BARBERSHOP, WITHIN 300 FEET OF A
  SIMILAR USE, IN AN EXISTING SHOPPING CENTER ON
  A C-2 (GENERAL COMMERCIAL) ZONED PROPERTY AT
  903 SOUTH PRAIRIE AVENUE.

Be approved.

The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

Ayes:  Commissioners Patrick, Rice, Trejo, Coleman and Chairman
  Springs.

Ms. Mindy Wilcox explained the appeal process.

6B: SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 2019-013 (SP-2019-013), 3320 WEST 85TH
STREET.
A public hearing to consider an application by Michael Zenon,
representing Faith Lutheran, for Special Use Permit No. 2019-013
(SP-2018-013) to allow a Preliminary Planned Assembly Development
(PAD) to allow a 65-unit senior housing mixed-use development on
a 26,250 square-foot C-2 (General Commercial)/Mixed-Use Overlay
zoned property at 3320 W. 85th Street.

Mr. Bernard McCrumby, Planner made the staff presentation.

Chairman Springs asked the Planning Commission if there were any
questions for staff.

Commissioner Patrick asked staff several questions:
 Wanted to know if there was a traffic study conducted for that
  site, with the Animo High School just west of the site, there
  is heavy vehicle traffic already in the area on Manchester
  Boulevard, 11th Avenue and 85th Street and there is also a post
  office across the street to the East of site.
 Her question was with regards to the Kiddie Kollege Day Care
  on the Southern Corner of 11th Avenue, will that child’s Day
  Care be closed once this project is complete?

  3
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 11, 2020
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that the Kiddie Kollege will remain after
  it is remodeled, along with the Senior Housing Mixed Use
  Development.
  Next to the large church on the corner is a smaller church or
  is it a banquet hall and are they connected?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated the building is connected to the Church,
  it is considered the Chapel area of the Church. The area that
  is behind the church, is going to be a part of the new
  development.

Commissioner Rice asked staff:
 From what is being presented, there is the possibility of tandem
  parking at the site. Is this what is included in the parking
  count or is there additional parking?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that the tandem parking is planned for
  eight parking spaces.
 With regards to Sunday Services for the parishioners, how would
  the valet parking be utilized?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that with regards to the valet service on
  Sundays, it will be located in the daycare playground area
  and will provide six parking spaces utilizing tandem parking
  configuration. It will be used for the church on Sundays.
 How many valet parking spaces will be utilized for the church
  on Sundays?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated twelve to fourteen parking spaces.
 What’s the seating capacity of the church?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that he does not have that information,
  but in City records for construction of the church, 38 parking
  spaces were required which is what the applicant will be
  providing and/or replacing as a part of this development.
 There are six deviations that the planning commission was asked
  to approve, have you calculated what if any will have a negative
  impact on the community?
  -  Mr. McCrumby stated that staff has not determined there would
  be a negative impact. In regards to open space, the applicant
  is providing 28 square feet less than what the code is
  requiring, but that is being replaced with some of the common
  area that the applicant is intending to provide with fitness
  classes, where the residents can come together and
  congregate. Another deviation request is the parking. The
  code requires one and a half parking spaces per unit, which
  would total 97 parking spaces and the applicant is providing
  65, so yes there is a slight reduction in the number of
  parking that would be required, but not one that would be too
  overwhelming for the nature of this type of development.
 Commissioner Rice stated that he was rather concerned that staff
  would want the Planning Commission to approve a project that is
  deficient by 45 parking spaces. Four or Five spaces is a minor
  deviation just one thing, but being deficient 45 parking spaces
  and do a trade with the church, for 38 parking spaces, but
  they’re still short 45. How does staff make this work?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that the deficiency is for the residential
  guest parking. The code requires 22 guest parking spaces, the
  applicant can provide 9 of the 22. The only reduction is with
  residential parking and nothing else.
 He asked if it was fair to not have enough guest parking spaces
  for the residents.
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that he could understand how the
  commissioner could be a bit concerned about the loss of
  parking spaces.

  4
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 11, 2020

Commissioner Rice posed a question to Chairman Springs –
 The people in that community have enjoyed being able to park on
  the street. Just adjacent to this project, there is the post
  office, the 99 cents store, other residential apartments, all
  who have had guests and visitors. Once the street is more
  impacted with this coming project, how do we accommodate the
  present residents?

Commissioner Rice asked staff –
 This new project will be built within a C-2 Zone, correct?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that is correct.
 The height maximum is 75 feet, correct?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that is correct.
 What is the present height for the parking section of this
  project? Sixty feet correct?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that is correct.
 Would it be possible for the applicant to go another 10 to 15
  feet in height, this would solve the parking problem and help
  to not impact the present community with the loss of street
  parking?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated yes, it most definitely would, but not
  sure of the cost ramifications to the applicant.
 Currently, our concern is with all of the residents who
  presently reside there in the neighborhood and need street
  parking.

Commissioner Trejo asked staff –
 Is the fact that some of the reduced parking is due to wanting
  to build senior citizen housing and low income housing, one of
  my initial concerns was what a way to insure that senior housing
  would be honored, but then I saw conditions nine and ten in the
  resolution and therefore that concern was addressed. But there
  is parking problems all over Inglewood. How far is this from a
  bus line or transportation?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that it is less than 1/2 a block to
  Manchester Blvd., and Eleventh Avenue.
 Another concern is the loading and unloading of children for
  the day care center and I’m hoping I’m not going to see a school
  car line stretched down to 85th street, for people dropping off
  and picking up kids.
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that he cannot speak to the current
  operation of the pre-school drop off, but I can say that on
  85th street there is a yellow street curb marker that is
  designed for loading and unloading of children.
 That is a concern. She stated that she believed in a lot of
  schools you get a parent who drops off their children, and they
  want to socialize with each other, because it causes gridlock
  and a backup of vehicles on the street waiting to drop off and
  pick up their children. She wants the applicant to speak to
  this.
 She would like to see how this is currently working and how
  after the build it will impact the school drop-offs and pick-
  ups. Would like the curbs to have signs saying no stopping or
  parking anytime.
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that if this project is approved, staff
  will be routing this project through the Public Works
  Division, so that Traffic will be able to take a look at this
  project and how it would relate to day to day issues with the
  pre-school children drop-offs and pick-ups.

  5
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 11, 2020

  Site is developed with the church and the pre-school only,
  correct? Please show on your slide presentation what is
  presently at the site and what will be demolished in order to
  make this new housing and parking with the church and school.
  - Mr. McCrumby presented the slides to the planning commission
  to show the layout and what the new project will entail.
  With the demolition and construction, will the size of the pre-
  school increase and will the number of students allowed to
  attend increase as well?
  - Mr. McCrumby referred the question to the applicant. He stated
  that the approximate size of the new pre-school will now be
  4,313 square feet.
  Would like to know how many children are presently in attendance
  and how many will be allowed to be in attendance once it is
  completed. How many will there be?
  Next question is what is the red-tiled building in the sketch?
  Is it coming down?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated it is the chapel at the church. Yes it
  is.

Commissioner Coleman stated to staff –
 His major concern was addressed by his colleague with regards
  to the number of students – how many currently are there and
  how many will be added or increased after the completion of the
  project.
 Next statement is in regards to the fact that two times a week
  there is street sweeping on 85th street and that will greatly
  impact the street parking issue for the current residents.
 What about the residential senior housing which will start at
  the third floor reaching up to the fifth floor and how it will
  impact the seniors, will there be elevators for them, what about
  those in wheelchairs, what about ADA consideration for the
  seniors who will be living there? What about getting to the
  parking area and to and from the resident dwellings to the
  ground level, are you saying the elevators are only for the use
  of the residents or all people on the property?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that the only people who need use of the
  elevators will be the residents and their guests. The first
  story will mainly be used for the pre-school and students,
  they will have no need to utilize the elevators.

Chairman Springs asked staff –
 When speaking about affordable housing, is staff speaking about
  affordable housing for seniors or affordable housing for the
  general public?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated it is all senior housing, but it would be
  senior market rate housing, the applicant would be offering
  a limited number of units for seniors with very low-income
  which then allows for additional units under their density
  bonus.

Chairman Springs stated that Commissioner Rice had a few questions
and after him Chairman Springs would close out the questions.

Commissioner Rice asked staff about –
 Code allows for concessions because the applicant is giving low
  income housing, but the City is already giving concessions with
  the density bonus of adding additional units, correct?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated the IMC allows for a density bonus for
  providing affordable housing, but it also allows, in addition
  to the density bonus, for code concessions that would allow
  the project to be more feasible, provide a lesser set-back or
  less parking or maybe “no” balconies or open space, etc.

  6
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 11, 2020

  But the density bonus that staff is offering with the additional
  units is by-right?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that it can be by-right, but in this
  instance the applicant is requesting it to be part of the
  PAD..
  But that density is not something that is before this planning
  commission body this evening?
  Mr. McCrumby stated that the PAD allows for 50 percent density
  bonus as part of the approval.

Chairman Springs asked staff about –
 So many one bedrooms and so many two bedrooms, and the one
  bedrooms, staff is stating it is open space?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that the one bedroom is an open floor
  plan. Yes.
 An Open floor plan by meaning that every unit has an open floor
  plan where there is no bedroom?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated not necessarily so. But there is a divided
  wall that provides for a bedroom.
 Staff wants to change the IMC requirements of 22 parking spaces
  to 9 parking spaces and why?
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that the reduction in guest parking is to
  allow the applicant to use what was originally approved for
  the required parking for the church.
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that the amount of parking proposed in this
  project is in line with other recent Senior projects that the
  City has approved such as Lime and Eucalyptus, which did not
  come before the planning commission because of the by-right
  density bonus, but in the case of that Senior Housing the
  parking required there in the end was about one-to-one, plus
  three or four visitor parking spaces for the forty units
  there.

Commissioner Rice asked staff about –
 Why was the site at Lime and Eucalyptus the by-right and not
  here on this project?
  - Ms. Wilcox stated that at that site, the applicant was asking
  for just the by-right density bonus for the requested
  concession, but in this case, the applicant is asking for the
  PAD.
 Can Staff or the applicant give the planning commission the full
  approximate cost of the construction on this project? The
  applicant will have to give a valuation at some point to the
  Building Department.
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that the applicant has given their
  valuation to the Building Department, but that he could not
  speak to the cost.
  - Mr. McCrumby stated that through the work that staff has
  already completed with the applicant, staff had asked the
  applicant to provide subterranean parking along with above
  the ground parking, and that had become cost prohibitive.
  However, the applicant will have to provide the cost number
  you are looking for.

Chairman Springs asked the applicant to come forward to address
the Planning Commission and speak about his project.

The applicant came before the planning commission to explain the
project, the parking situation, their ideas and solutions which
one idea is that the shared parking is only on Sundays during
service times, and one idea is to have valet parking on Sundays
for the parishioners and to utilize the school yard for the
vehicles that may attend Sunday Service. With regards to the

  7
 Inglewood Special Planning Commission Meeting Minutes
March 11, 2020
dropping off and picking up of children during the week, it will
be the same process as before, adding nothing more to the traffic.
Chairman Springs opened the floor to the Planning Commissioners
with questions for the applicant.

Commissioner Patrick asked the applicant –
 A church and a pre-school – how does that work? The reason for
  the church keeping the pre-school and opening of the Senior
  Housing?
  - Mr. Zenon stated that the pre-school is a part of the Lutheran
  Church program to reach the community. The Lutheran Church
  feels that it is a great program there at the Lutheran Church
  with the mixing of the two generations.
 She feels this is a great idea. One major concern is the parking
  situation in the area.
  - Mr. Zenon stated that through their analysis of the parking
  situation in the area they considered the drop-off and pickup
  of pre-school children at Kiddie Kollege, traffic for the
  Post Office across the street going east on 85th street, the
  residents in the apartment complex on the north side of 85th
  street, the motorcycle training which is more than a block
  and a half to the east, and the Animo High School that is a
  block west of our project. So, in looking at the parking
  situation there at the corner of 85th and 11th Avenue,
  regarding the church’s parking on Sundays, the Kiddie Kollege
  stated the church is more than welcome to utilize their
  parking area and playground area for additional parking for
  the church on Sundays. With regards to the picking up and
  dropping off of children for the Kiddie Kollege during the
  week, in order to not pose a strain on 11th Avenue and 85th
  Street, the parents will arrive very early in the mornings
  prior to the Animo school hours, and then retrieve their
  children in the middle of the day while the Animo school is
  still open for school hours. With regards to the residents to
  the north of the church, during the day time, several of the
  residents are not home during that time of the day, so there
  is little to no impact there.

Commissioner Rice asked the applicant –
 With regards to the church utilizing the parking lots in the
  area, there has to be a covenant between the church and those
  entities, the Animo Charter High School, the Kiddie Kollege and
  the City for the open parking lot use by the church, will the
  church be willing to do this?
  - Mr. Zenon stated that it will be no problem in having a
  covenant drawn up and signed by the church and these other
  entities, as in the past the church has always had a great
  relationship with the schools in the area regarding
  additional church parking.
 What is the cost of this project at present?
  - Mr. Zenon stated the cost so far is $16 to $20 Million.
 Generally, when an applicant is asking for a variance on parking
  it is because the area is land-locked by the code, there is no
  other parking available in the area, the parking has height
  restrictions or land availability restrictions. In this case
  that is not the situation, as your project can either do
